{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — RadialSpark Consulting Agreement (Clear Capital as Customer)

## Executive Summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. The commercial architecture is favourable in several important respects: there is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum purchase commitment, no MFN obligation, no auto-renewal mechanic, no liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, and no Vendor audit right over our records. Those points are compliant and require no redline.

The risk is concentrated in three critical areas. First, the Agreement contains **no indemnity at all** — Section 7's heading refers to "Indemnification of Contractor", but the section consists solely of liability caps, a consequential damages waiver and an attorneys' fees waiver. Second, **ownership of the Works is fragmented invoice-by-invoice**: Section 4(a) vests the Works in the Company only to the extent created in a period that has been invoiced and paid, with no present assignment and no interim licence, and the Agreement nowhere confirms that we retain ownership of our own data and pre-existing materials. Third, the **limitation of liability fails the fallback**: its only stated exception cross-references "Paragraph 9", which is the Independent Contractor clause, so no carve-out is operative for confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement, and Contractor's cap is limited to fees actually paid under the relevant Statement of Work.

High-severity items follow the same theme of one-sided exit and transfer rights: we have **no convenience-termination right over an in-flight Statement of Work** (Section 6(a) is available only when no SOW is outstanding), and every Company assignment — including to an affiliate or a successor in a merger — requires Contractor consent. At medium severity we address the absence of any post-termination transition assistance or data return, the absence of any conformance warranty or remedy (with implied warranties disclaimed under Section 5(e)), Arizona governing law, and a missing general-advertising carve-out in the mutual non-solicit. At low severity, the existing insurance covenant omits cyber/privacy coverage entirely for a vendor that accesses our systems and data.

Two items are marked for reviewer sign-off rather than asserted as clean: the audit position and the licence-grant scope under Section 4(c).

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 7 (Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor) | No operative indemnity language anywhere; Section 7 is caps and waivers only. Section 5(c) gives a non-infringement warranty, not a defence obligation. Walk-away territory. Proposed new § 7(d) Contractor indemnity (third-party IP, breach of law, data/confidentiality breach, wilful misconduct) with notice/control/cooperation mechanics and a carve-out from the § 7 limitations. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 4 (Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance) | § 4(a) vests Works only "to the extent" created in an invoiced-and-paid period; no present assignment, no interim licence. § 4(d) defers our right to modify until payment in full. No statement that we retain ownership of our data and pre-existing materials. § 4(b) and the § 4(c) licence-back are acceptable and unchanged. Proposal: present assignment on creation plus a Customer Data/materials ownership sentence. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 7 | Cap and consequential-damages exclusion are nominally mutual, but the sole exception cross-references Paragraph 9 (Independent Contractor) and is inoperative — no carve-out for confidentiality (§ 8), gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement or indemnification. Contractor's cap is limited to fees actually paid under the relevant SOW. Proposal: mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with standard uncapped Excluded Claims and confirmation that fee obligations are not capped damages. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 10 (via § 7 review) | No change-of-control provision (acceptable), but all Company assignments — including to affiliates and to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets — require Contractor consent. Reasonableness qualifier does not cure the absence of an M&A/affiliate carve-out. Proposal: add affiliate/successor carve-out and bar assignment to a Company competitor; mutual reasonable-consent standard otherwise intact. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 6 (Termination) | Term is indefinite; the only convenience right (§ 6(a)) applies solely when no uncompleted SOW is outstanding, so we cannot exit an in-flight engagement, and there is no refund mechanic for prepaid amounts. Vendor side is already at our preferred position. Proposal: minimal edit adding a Company right to terminate the Agreement or any SOW on 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid fees for Services not performed. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 1 (Purpose of Engagement) | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation; Services engaged "on a task by task basis" under separate SOWs. The three uses of "exclusive" are an ownership allocation, a non-exclusive grant in our favour, and entire-agreement boilerplate. No redline. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 6 (Termination) | No liquidated damages, penalty, kill fee, minimum fee or early-termination charge. § 6(a), § 6(b) and the § 7(c) wind-down entitle Contractor only to fees and expenses accrued through termination. Noted only: § 3(b) permits uncapped rate changes on 30 days' notice — a pricing point under other rules. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 7 review scope | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binding us. § 13 is a mutual employee-only non-solicit; the § 4 resale restriction protects Contractor background IP and is a scope-of-licence term, not a field-of-use restraint. No redline. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 11 (via § 7 review) | Arizona law, no venue specified; outside the accepted list (New York preferred; Delaware, California, England and Wales at fallback). Arbitration clause is US-administered with confirmation in US courts, so not walk-away. Proposal: New York law plus exclusive New York County venue for proceedings not resolved by arbitration; severability language preserved. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Missing | § 6 (Termination) | § 6 covers only notice, final fees and assignment of title to Works in progress. No transition assistance, no return of Company data/Works/Confidential Information, no deletion or certification; the confidentiality clause has no return mechanic. Proposal: new § 6(d) — up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, return within 30 days in machine-readable format, certified deletion; 90 days' assistance acceptable as fallback. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5 (Representations and Warranties; Warranty Disclaimer) | Warranties cover only legal compliance (knowledge-qualified), rights/authority and non-infringement, plus anti-bribery. No conformance warranty, no warranty period, no repair/re-perform/refund remedy; § 1(b) is a bare workmanlike covenant and § 5(e) disclaims implied warranties. Proposal: 90-day conformance warranty for Services and Works with re-performance, repair/replacement or refund, and confirmation that express warranties survive the disclaimer. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 13 (via § 7 review) | Mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, one year post-termination, solicitation-based — otherwise at fallback. No carve-out for general advertising or unsolicited approaches, so ordinary recruiting or an inbound approach could breach it. Proposal: add the customary carve-out sentence only; duration and scope untouched. |
| Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 3 (Contractor's Compensation) | No most-favoured-nation, benchmarking or price-matching covenant anywhere. Nothing to redline. § 3(b) uncapped rate change noted for information only. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant | § 3 (Contractor's Compensation) | No minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall, guaranteed-hours or volume obligation; strictly time and materials per SOW plus actual expenses, with a 15-day convenience exit when no SOW is outstanding. No redline. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 1 (Purpose of Engagement) | No auto-renewal mechanic (the word "renew" does not appear). Term runs until terminated, with a 15-day either-party exit under § 6(a) when no SOW is outstanding — better than our preferred 30 days. No renewal uplift to cap. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review | § 3 (Contractor's Compensation) | Assessed as compliant with no redline: the Agreement grants Contractor no audit, inspection or records-examination right. § 3(b) is a one-way invoicing-detail obligation on Contractor; § 1(c) access provisions run in our favour. Total absence is better than our preferred position, and proposing a redline would create a Vendor right that does not exist. Flagged for sign-off because the deterministic "audit frequency limited" check fails only for want of any audit right to cap. Watch item: apply preferred limits if a future SOW introduces a verification right. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation | § 7 para 14 | Covenant exists and delivers workers' compensation as required by statute, CGL of USD 1,000,000, E&O of USD 1,000,000 (fallback level) and certificates on request with notice of material change — but no cyber/privacy coverage at any level. Material because § 8 defines Confidential Information to include our data and records held by Contractor and § 1(c) contemplates access to our facilities and systems. Proposal: insert a cyber/privacy limb at USD 5,000,000 where Contractor processes Company data; USD 2,000,000 offered as fallback. Noted only: no CGL aggregate stated, E&O below preferred USD 2M, self-insurance permitted. |
| Low | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Needs review | § 4 (Ownership of Materials; Acceptance) | Substance is at or above fallback: § 4(c) grants a royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual licence with no revocation or clawback and a broad "business operations" scope. Affiliates and contractors are nowhere named ("Affiliate" does not appear), so their coverage rests on reading the unconditional sublicence right as self-executing — a phrasing variant, hence sign-off. Optional clarifying edit: name Affiliates and contractors, add "irrevocable", confirm transfer to a successor. Grant runs in our favour; not to be pressed hard. |

## Walk-Away Items

1. **No Vendor indemnity (INDEMN, § 7).** The complete absence of any defence or indemnity obligation — no IP indemnity, and nothing for breach of law, data/confidentiality breach or wilful misconduct — fails even the fallback and sits in walk-away territory. This must be resolved before signature, and the indemnity must be carved out of the § 7 limitations so it is not neutralised by the fees-paid cap and the attorneys' fees waiver.
2. **Ownership of the Works (IP, § 4(a)/(d)).** Title fragmented invoice-by-invoice, with no present assignment and no interim licence, means any unbilled, unpaid or disputed period leaves work we commissioned owned by Contractor with no rights back to us — below the fallback, which requires a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense. Compounded by § 4(d) deferring our modification right until payment in full and by the absence of any Customer Data ownership statement.
3. **Liability carve-outs (LOL-CAP, § 7(a)).** With the sole exception pointing at the Independent Contractor clause, no carve-out survives for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct — the minimum set required at fallback. Combined with items 1 and 2, this leaves us without a remedy for the exposures that matter most.

*Related and near the walk-away line:* the missing cyber/privacy insurance limb (INSURANCE) is described as approaching walk-away concern given Contractor's access to our data and systems, and should be settled alongside the indemnity.

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the three critical items (new § 7(d) Contractor indemnity carved out of § 7; present assignment of the Works plus Customer Data ownership; mutual 12-months'-fees/USD 1M cap with standard uncapped Excluded Claims) as a single non-severable package.
2. **Press the two high-severity structural points:** a Company convenience right over the Agreement and any SOW on 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid fees, and the affiliate/successor assignment carve-out with a bar on assignment to a Company competitor.
3. **Land the medium items** in one pass: New York law and exclusive New York County venue; new § 6(d) transition assistance, 30-day return in machine-readable format and certified deletion (90 days' assistance acceptable); 90-day conformance warranty with repair/re-perform/refund; and the general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs to § 13.
4. **Add the cyber/privacy insurance limb** at USD 5,000,000 where Contractor processes Company data, with USD 2,000,000 as the landing zone; leave the balance of the insurance covenant untouched.
5. **Obtain reviewer sign-off on the two needs-review items.** Confirm we take no redline on audit (proposing one would create a Vendor right that does not presently exist) and decide whether to run the optional § 4(c) licence clarification, which we will not press if resisted.
6. **Flag the SOW watch item** to the business: because the commercial substance sits in Statements of Work, future SOWs should be reviewed for any usage-verification or records-examination right, and for the uncapped § 3(b) rate-change mechanic, which our 15-day no-SOW exit only partially mitigates."}
